hotspots.title: Javier Milei’s corruption scandal engulfs top aide
hotspots.blurb: Argentine prosecutor Pollicita ordered ex-Chief of Staff Manuel Adorni to justify his and his family’s wealth within 15 days over alleged illicit enrichment. Over 20 articles detail the legal summons, asset discrepancies, and political fallout, with the case threatening to undermine Milei’s anti-corruption platform.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to its moral panic framing, polarized contention between Milei’s government and opposition, and the high stakes of a corruption scandal in a self-proclaimed libertarian administration.

hotspots.title: Vox’s constitutional crusade against Spain’s PM over Ceuta
hotspots.blurb: Vox escalates its campaign against Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, demanding the activation of Article 102 of Spain’s Constitution for alleged treason over the Ceuta migrant crisis. The party frames the situation as an 'act of war' and pressures the PP to join its legal offensive, while also opposing the distribution of unaccompanied migrant minors across Spanish regions.
hotspots.affect: This hotspot is charged due to its alarmist framing of migration as a national security threat, moral outrage over alleged government negligence, and the high-stakes political maneuvering to impeach Sánchez.

hotspots.title: AfD’s surge in German state elections
hotspots.blurb: The Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) leads polls in Saxony-Anhalt with 42%, threatening an absolute majority in the upcoming September elections. The party’s rise is framed as a rejection of the 'firewall' strategy against it, with economists warning of 'catastrophic' economic consequences if AfD implements its policies.
hotspots.affect: This commands attention due to its alarmist framing of AfD’s potential victory, polarized contention over migration and economic policies, and the high stakes of far-right governance in Germany.

hotspots.title: Tisza Party’s presidential pick sparks constitutional crisis
hotspots.blurb: Hungary’s Tisza Party nominated former Supreme Court President András Baka as its presidential candidate, sparking a constitutional crisis. The nomination is framed as a rejection of Orbán’s legacy, with Fidesz boycotting the process and accusing the Tisza Party of undermining democratic institutions. The crisis highlights tensions over judicial independence and the rule of law.
hotspots.affect: This commands attention due to its framing as a constitutional crisis, polarized contention over judicial independence, and the high stakes of Hungary’s political future under the Tisza Party.

hotspots.affect: This commands attention due to its alarmist framing of prison overcrowding, polarized contention over immigration, and the moral outrage over human rights concerns.
